seo.description: Essaouira guide: UNESCO medina, Skala, fishing port, Atlantic beach, Mellah and Gnaoua spirit. When to visit, what to see and day trips on the windy coast.

name: Essaouira
hero_subtitle: Atlantic trade winds, a white-and-blue UNESCO medina, Skala cannons facing the ocean and a lively fishing port — Morocco’s windiest and most photogenic coastal city.

overview.title: Welcome to Essaouira — Wind, Walls and Atlantic Light
overview.p1: Essaouira sits on Morocco’s Atlantic coast, about two and a half hours west of Marrakech. Its medina is UNESCO-listed: straight streets, whitewashed walls, blue shutters and the Skala ramparts lined with historic cannons facing the waves.
overview.p2: The lively fishing port, long beach, craft souks and the Purple Islands offshore give the town a balanced rhythm — walls you can walk, fresh seafood at the port, and steady trade winds that made it a global destination for water sports and artists.
overview.p3: Come for the bright light, quiet port mornings and Skala walks. Two or three nights are enough to enjoy the beach and a day trip into the countryside or nearby coastal villages.

places.title: Places to visit in Essaouira
places.subtitle: Historic city walls, active port life and Atlantic sands.

medina.title: Medina & Walls
medina.desc: White-and-blue UNESCO medina with geometric streets and defensive walls on the sea.

skala_ville.title: Skala de la Ville
skala_ville.desc: Famous cannon platform above the ocean — Essaouira’s best-known sunset viewpoint.

skala_port.title: Skala du Port
skala_port.desc: Fortified port bastion with striking views over boats and islands.

port.title: Fishing Port
port.desc: Harbour busy with traditional blue boats, morning catch and fresh grilled fish.

plage.title: Essaouira Beach
plage.desc: Wide Atlantic sand strip ideal for walking, kitesurfing and sunset (often windy).

mellah.title: Mellah
mellah.desc: Lanes of the historic Jewish quarter that add depth to the town fabric.

iles.title: Purple Islands
iles.desc: Rocky islands offshore — views from the Skala or a short boat trip when conditions allow.

souks.title: Souks & Craft Quarter
souks.desc: Thuya wood workshops, silver and fragrant spice lanes inside the medina.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-Day Plan in Essaouira
itinerary.subtitle: Ramparts and port first, then beach and islands, with quiet time for souks and crafts.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Enter the white-and-blue UNESCO medina; walk the Skala de la Ville overlooking the Atlantic.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Visit the fishing port and blue boats, then climb the Skala du Port for cannons and sea views.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Stroll the old Jewish quarter lanes and enjoy fresh seafood near the port or in a traditional riad.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Walk the long Atlantic sands south of the walls — or watch kite surfers and water sports.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Explore thuya wood workshops, silver and spice lanes inside the medina.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Return to the Skala for the wind and golden light over the islands.
detailed_itinerary.day3_m: Morning — Purple Islands or Free Walk
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Boat trip to the Purple Islands (sea conditions permitting), or a quiet morning in the medina lanes.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: More beach time, or a short visit to Diabat village and the nearby coastal dunes.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Last walk at the port, then ready for Marrakech or Agadir.

stays.title: Where to stay in Essaouira? Our favourites
stays.subtitle: Historic riads in the medina, ocean-view hotels and charming guesthouses: discover our recommended addresses for an unforgettable stay in Essaouira.

card1.name: Hotel Vue Skala
card1.desc: Looks straight onto the historic Atlantic walls, with water views and authentic Moroccan comfort.

card2.name: Villa Atlantique
card2.desc: Quiet retreat in the white-and-blue medina lanes, with a bright courtyard and a terrace for relaxing.

card3.name: Riad Les Remparts
card3.desc: Combines historic charm with modern facilities, perfectly placed a few steps from the fishing port.

card4.name: Hotel Medina
card4.desc: Just outside the walls facing the ocean swell — ideal for open space and water sports.

booking_banner.desc: Compare live prices, read trusted reviews and discover more riads, apartments and beach hotels via Booking.com.

eat.title: Where to eat in Essaouira
eat.subtitle: Fresh grilled fish at the port, medina tables and beach cafés.

nomad.title: Port Grill
nomad.desc: Busy popular tables at midday when the fishing boats come in.

jardin.title: Beach Cafés
jardin.desc: Light food and drinks on the Atlantic strip.

moha.title: Hotel Restaurants
moha.desc: Reliable, refined dining options near the walls.

fassia.title: Medina Cafés
fassia.desc: Enjoyable daily coffee sessions away from the beach bustle.

elfenn.title: Tajines & Salads
elfenn.desc: Varied traditional Moroccan dishes alongside seafood.

bacha.title: Evening Dinner
bacha.desc: Relaxed atmosphere and later service once the evening wind eases.

transport.title: Getting around
transport.desc: The medina is fully walkable. Petit taxis for the beach strip and bus station; agree prices in advance for longer coastal hops.

bargain.title: Wind & sun
bargain.desc: Trade winds are part of the town’s character — bring a light jacket even in summer, and high-SPF protection on the Skala and beach.

water.title: Tickets & cash
water.desc: Most sights and paths inside the medina are free. Carry dirhams for taxis, port meals and souk purchases.

daytrips.title: Best day trips from Essaouira
daytrips.subtitle: Coastal beaches, quiet villages and distinctive landscapes.

sidi_kaouki.title: Sidi Kaouki
sidi_kaouki.desc: Beach known for its sports and quiet surf vibe about 25 minutes south.

diabat.title: Diabat
diabat.desc: Quiet village and charming dunes close to town.

marrakech.title: Marrakech
marrakech.desc: Historic city and traditional souks about two and a half hours east.

argan.title: Coastal Argan Country
argan.desc: Rural roads rich in argan trees and Atlantic viewpoints.

q1.question: How many days are enough for Essaouira?
q1.answer: Two full days cover the medina, Skala, port and beach at a comfortable pace. Three days allow a slower rhythm and a coastal day trip.

q2.question: Is Essaouira very windy?
q2.answer: Yes — the trade winds are central to its identity; great for atmosphere and wind sports, but bring a light jacket for the ramparts.

q3.question: How do I get to Essaouira?
q3.answer: Essaouira Airport (ESU) has seasonal flights; regular buses and private transfers also link it with Marrakech (about 2.5 h) and Casablanca.

q4.question: What is the best time to visit?
q4.answer: Spring and early autumn bring milder climate and wind. Summer is lively and active but windy; winter is quieter and cooler.

q5.question: Is the beach good for swimming?
q5.answer: The beach is excellent for long walks and water sports; swimming depends directly on swell and wind strength, so check local conditions.
